subject: economics

concepts.title: Cobb-Douglas and Algebraic Production Function Evaluation
concepts.definition: The mathematical rule that specifies the greatest attainable output level corresponding to distinct combinations of factor inputs under a set state of technological knowledge.
concepts.key_idea: Input quantities are plugged into the production equation to obtain the maximum physical yield.
question_patterns: calculate the maximum output produced for given units of labour and capital
find the total yield when labour is ... and capital is ...
compute the output from the production function
determine the quantity produced by employing ... units of labour and ... units of capital
what is the maximum possible output given the factor inputs

solution_steps.action: evaluate output by substituting input levels into the production function
solution_steps.explain: multiply the scale factor with labour raised to its exponent and capital raised to its exponent

concepts.title: Average Product of a Variable Factor
concepts.definition: The per-unit output generated by a variable input factor while keeping the amounts of all remaining production inputs unaltered.
concepts.key_idea: Total product divided by the quantity of the variable input employed.
question_patterns: find the average product of labour
calculate average product when total product is ... and labour is ...
what is the AP of labour for an output of ... with ... workers
determine the output per unit of labour employed
compute the average physical product

solution_steps.action: divide total output by variable factor units
solution_steps.explain: average product represents output generated per worker

concepts.title: Marginal Product of a Variable Factor
concepts.definition: The increment in aggregate physical output resulting from the addition of one extra unit of the variable input, holding fixed inputs constant.
concepts.key_idea: Difference between total output at current employment and total output at the preceding employment level.
question_patterns: calculate the marginal product of the nth worker
find marginal product when total product changes from ... to ...
what is the MP of labour at ... units of employment
determine the addition to total product made by hiring an extra worker
compute the marginal physical return to labour

solution_steps.action: subtract previous total product from current total product
solution_steps.explain: marginal product equals the change in output for a single unit change in input

concepts.title: Total Product Derived from Average Product
concepts.definition: The overall volume of goods manufactured by a firm through employing a specified quantity of a variable resource alongside constant inputs.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying output per unit by total units of the variable resource yields total production.
question_patterns: find the total product given average product and labour
calculate total product when AP is ... and labour employed is ...
what is the aggregate output if each worker produces an average of ... units
determine the total physical product from average product
how much total output is produced by ... workers with an AP of ...

solution_steps.action: multiply average product by the number of labour units
solution_steps.explain: total physical product is the product of average output per unit and total units used

concepts.title: Law of Variable Proportions and Diminishing Marginal Returns
concepts.definition: The economic tendency wherein increasing successive units of a variable factor to fixed factors initially causes marginal additions to rise, but eventually causes marginal product to diminish.
concepts.formula: MP initially rises, attains maximum, and subsequently falls
concepts.key_idea: Varying factor proportions leads from underutilization to crowding of the fixed resource.
question_patterns: explain the law of variable proportions
why does the marginal product of labour eventually decline
state the law of diminishing marginal product
describe the three phases of production in the short run
what happens to total product when marginal product is negative

solution_steps.action: identify the initial stage of increasing marginal returns
solution_steps.explain: better utilization of fixed factor and specialization lead to rising MP

solution_steps.action: identify the point of diminishing marginal returns
solution_steps.explain: crowding of the fixed factor causes additions to total output to decline

concepts.title: Returns to Scale in Production
concepts.definition: The proportional behavior of output when all productive inputs are simultaneously scaled up by an identical proportion in the long run.
concepts.formula: CRS if f(tL, tK) = t*f(L,K); IRS if f(tL, tK) > t*f(L,K); DRS if f(tL, tK) < t*f(L,K)
concepts.key_idea: Returns to scale depend on whether output expands proportionally, more than proportionally, or less than proportionally relative to all inputs.
question_patterns: when does a production function exhibit constant returns to scale
distinguish between increasing, constant and decreasing returns to scale
what returns to scale are exhibited if doubling inputs triples output
verify the nature of returns to scale for the Cobb-Douglas function
explain why long run returns to scale differ from short run returns to a factor

solution_steps.action: evaluate output scaling factor relative to input multiplier
solution_steps.explain: if sum of powers alpha + beta equals 1 it is CRS, greater than 1 is IRS, less than 1 is DRS

concepts.title: Short-Run Total Cost
concepts.definition: The aggregate expenditure incurred by an enterprise to produce a specified level of output, comprising both fixed expenses and variable operating expenses.
concepts.key_idea: Total cost is the sum of total fixed cost and total variable cost.
question_patterns: calculate total cost when TFC is ... and TVC is ...
find total cost for an output given fixed cost and variable cost
compute the short run total expenditure of producing ... units
determine TC from total fixed cost and total variable cost
what is the total cost when TVC equals ... and fixed obligations equal ...

solution_steps.action: sum fixed cost and variable cost
solution_steps.explain: total cost includes all outlays on both fixed and variable factors

concepts.title: Average Fixed Cost
concepts.definition: The fixed expenditure allocated per unit of physical output produced in the short run.
concepts.key_idea: Fixed cost divided by output quantity, forming a rectangular hyperbola.
question_patterns: find average fixed cost when TFC is ... and output is ...
calculate AFC at ... units of production
what is the average fixed cost for an output level of ...
determine the per unit fixed cost when total fixed cost equals ...
compute AFC given fixed cost and quantity

solution_steps.action: divide total fixed cost by output quantity
solution_steps.explain: average fixed cost diminishes continuously as output increases

concepts.title: Average Variable Cost
concepts.definition: The variable expenditure incurred per unit of output generated by the enterprise.
concepts.key_idea: Total variable cost divided by total output.
question_patterns: calculate average variable cost when TVC is ... and output is ...
find AVC at ... units of output
what is the per-unit variable cost for producing ... units
determine average variable cost given total variable cost
compute AVC when output is ... and variable outlay is ...

solution_steps.action: divide total variable cost by output quantity
solution_steps.explain: average variable cost is obtained by dividing TVC by total units produced

concepts.title: Short-Run Average Cost
concepts.definition: The overall cost per unit of output produced in the short run, equal to the sum of average fixed and average variable costs.
concepts.key_idea: Total cost divided by output level, or the sum of AFC and AVC.
question_patterns: calculate short run average cost when TC is ... and output is ...
find SAC at ... units of production
what is the average cost of producing ... units given total cost ...
determine short run average cost per unit of output
compute SAC from total cost and quantity

solution_steps.action: divide total cost by output volume
solution_steps.explain: average cost represents the full unit cost of production at that output level

concepts.title: Short-Run Marginal Cost
concepts.definition: The net addition to total cost (or total variable cost) caused by the manufacture of one supplementary unit of output.
concepts.key_idea: Incremental cost of producing the next unit of output.
question_patterns: calculate short run marginal cost when total cost increases from ... to ...
find SMC for the nth unit of output
what is the marginal cost of producing the ...th unit
determine SMC given total cost schedule
compute the addition to total cost for one extra unit of output

solution_steps.action: subtract previous total cost from current total cost
solution_steps.explain: marginal cost equals the change in total cost for a single unit change in output

concepts.title: Geometric Relationships Among Short-Run and Long-Run Cost Curves
concepts.definition: The structural geometric properties where marginal cost curves intersect average cost and average variable cost curves from below at their respective minimum points.
concepts.formula: SMC = AVC at min(AVC); SMC = SAC at min(SAC); LRMC = LRAC at min(LRAC)
concepts.key_idea: When average cost is falling, marginal cost lies below it; when average cost is rising, marginal cost lies above it.
question_patterns: why does SMC cut AVC at its lowest point
at what point does the SMC curve intersect the SAC curve
explain the relationship between average cost and marginal cost
describe the shape of the average fixed cost curve
why are short run and long run average cost curves U-shaped

solution_steps.action: state the condition where average cost is at its minimum
solution_steps.explain: as long as marginal cost is below average cost, average cost falls; when marginal cost is above average cost, average cost rises, making the intersection occur at the minimum point
